simple.meaning: מִדָּה (middâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “tribute in money.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 4:13. Its contexts include Torah, kingship, priesthood, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִדָּה (H4061).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מִדָּה (middâh) / H4061 is traced through Ezra 4:13, Ezra 4:20, Ezra 6:8, Ezra 7:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4061. middah or mindah מִדָּה מִנְדָּה, (?) noun feminine tribute (Assyrian loan-word, compare Biblical Hebrew II. [ מִדָּה ]); — absolute ׳מִנ Ezra 4:13 ; 7:24 + 4:20 Baer (van d. H. Gi Str מִדָּה ); construct מִדַּת 6:8 . מַנְדַּע see ידע .

occurrences.englishText: Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the kings.
There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll, was paid to them.

Moreover I make a decree what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that they not be hindered.
Also we inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tribute, custom, or toll, on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or laborers of this house of God.
